author: Michal238
text:
One week ago I decided to finally figure out how IF draw these blue boxes and how to apply it into trading:

 www.forexfactory.com/attachment.php?atta...1423315&d=1399633037

After intense price reading sessions I had yesterday few eureka moments. My price reading skills definitely improved.

These boxes can be drawn on any TF and they are really great tool. What
they show is nothing new but it helped me to see price in different way -
 as zones.

Edges of this zones are flag limits / FTRs.

After price break flag limit/FTR new one is created.

FO from this zone is often great QM lvl.

I did analysis of NZDUSD. I tried to get into mind of ITs, I used some boxes and concepts I learned before.

author: naascott
text:
Hi Michal,

Well stated. Your journal has been refreshing to follow. I wish you the best of success.

Perhaps start out with micro lots, a good trade management plan (you
stick to as if your life depends on it) and see how you react.

I know what it is like to trade real money . Each person is different I
suppose. At least for me, trading real money introduced me to myself
very quickly, and I did not like the person I met. Like many poor
newbs, I was completely oblivious to the realities of trading, and had
my butt handed to me on more than one occasion. I often found myself
giving back any and all profits, and then moving into revenge mode only
 to sustain even larger losses. I was probably part of the stupidest
crowd of traders there were. Had money, but no plan, no experience -
basically all the makings of someone bound for the 95% group of sunken
traders.

Thankfully, through much pain, reading and perseverance, I started to
see the possibility that I could actually succeed as a trader. However, I
 was still lacking something. I just knew it! But I could not quite put
my finger on it. To make a long story short, it was a place like this
that I was lacking. I have found no other place that helps a guy/gal really make sense of what is going on in price. Seiden is great and does a nice job, but I love the hands we are in here at RTM.

Much success to you, Michal.

P.S. I recently started reading "Trading in the Zone" by M. Douglas.
Interesting read on the psychological side of things in trading.

Thank you guys for advice, I really appreciate that .

I'll definitely set myself some rules to follow. I belive that the most
important thing is to take only the best setups with high RR, this gives
 huge statistical advantage.

It is also difficult thing to do because it is frustrating when you
don't enter and then it goes in my direction as I predicted. But this is
 part of trading and in the long run letting go not so perfect setups is
 beneficial. I'll focus on that to avoid overtrading which is what I'm
most afraid of.
